subject: Hosted API rates + model compatibility scan request
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@healthmetrics.ai>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-20T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Quick ask — per-1M IO rates and model roster for hosted API

Hi Naomi,

We’re kicking off a small pilot at HealthMetrics.ai to add LLM-driven summarization to our provider dashboards and I'm pulling together baseline unit economics. Could you send over your standard per-1M token rates (input / output split) for the hosted API and the list of models you publish for general availability (note whether a model is recommended for chat/conversational workloads vs. short-form completion)?

A few specifics that would help:
- Baseline rates (per 1M input tokens / per 1M output tokens) for the typical model tiers (small / medium / large)
- Any trial credits or standard pilot discounts you offer for new customers
- Model family names and a one-line guidance on latency/cost tradeoffs (we care about 100-300ms median latency if possible)

We're aiming for a 10M token pilot footprint over three months as a first pass. If you can include any suggested model for an extractive summarization workflow, that would be great.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of AI, HealthMetrics.ai
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@healthmetrics.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-20T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask — per-1M IO rates and model roster for hosted API

Hi Samir,

Thanks for the note and congrats on getting the pilot scoped. I've attached our Q4 rate card (PDF) and a short matrix below to get you started. I'll loop in Aditya on the discounts/commit terms; Ben is on cc for latency/engineering pointers.

Baseline hosted API IO rates (standard, non-committed):
- Redwood-7B (small): Input $0.60 / 1M tokens, Output $1.20 / 1M tokens
- Redwood-14B (medium): Input $1.20 / 1M tokens, Output $2.40 / 1M tokens
- Redwood-70B (large): Input $3.50 / 1M tokens, Output $7.00 / 1M tokens

Model guidance (high level):
- Redwood-7B: cost-efficient for high-throughput short completions, decent for extractive summarization but watch for hallucinations on long context.
- Redwood-14B: recommended default for chat-like summarization where latency around 200-400ms is acceptable; best balance of cost/quality for many prod use cases.
- Redwood-70B: top-tier quality for complex reasoning but significantly higher cost and latency; generally used for high-value responses or reranking.

Pilot notes: for a 10M token/month pilot we often recommend Redwood-14B quantized to INT8 for a good latency/cost tradeoff. Standard pilots get a one-time $5,000 evaluation credit (applied to hosted usage) and a short-term promotional discount we can stack with commits. Please see the attached rate card for full model listings and supported endpoints.

I've attached:
- Redwood_Hosted_Rate_Card_Q4_2026.pdf (rate table + model roster)

Next steps: if you'd like, we can set up a 30-minute call this week to map the pilot profile (input vs. output token ratio, expected concurrency) so Ben can recommend batching and KV caching settings.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Samir/Team,

Quick add on discounts / commitments: the public rates Naomi pasted are our list (non-committed) prices. Standard volume discount schedule we offer for hosted API commitments is below (we're flexible on structuring a short pilot carve-out):

Volume (monthly tokens) => Standard discount off list
- 0-9M => 0%
- 10M-49M => 5%
- 50M-199M => 10%
- 200M+ => 20% (or discuss a dedicated reservation for predictable throughput and lower unit cost)

Pilot incentives:
- One-time $5k evaluation credit for new accounts (applies to hosted usage)
- For pilots that convert to an annual committed path within 60 days we can extend an additional 10% credit for the first three billing cycles (subject to approval)

Operational notes (Ben)
- Ben: see Ben's suggestions in the attached CSV on expected latency when using INT8 quantization vs float16 for the 14B family; caching prefix keys aggressively can reduce output token costs for summarization workflows.

I've uploaded a short discount schedule and the DocuSign link for our standard MSA if you want to move quickly.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Samir
